title: Two Knights Defence
intro: 3...Nf6: guard e4 with 4.d3, castle, and meet each Black plan calmly.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 g8f6

lessons.title: 4.d3 and the slow build-up
lessons.summary: Guard e4, castle, then c3, h3 and Re1.

steps.text: 3...Nf6 is the Two Knights Defence. It attacks your e4 pawn at once.
Protect e4 the quiet way.
steps.hint: A one-square pawn move guards e4.
steps.ifWrong: 4.d3 guards e4, so the knight has nothing to take.
steps.ifRight: The quiet plan: castle, play c3, and push d4 only when you are ready.

feedback.f3g5: 4.Ng5 is a sharp, famous attack. This repertoire stays calm with 4.d3.
feedback.b1c3: 4.Nc3 also guards e4, but this repertoire plays 4.d3.
feedback.e1g1: Castling first is playable, but this repertoire guards e4 first with 4.d3.
feedback.d2d4: 4.d4 opens the game sharply. This repertoire keeps it calm with 4.d3.

steps.text: 4...Bc5 develops the bishop towards f2.
Castle first.
steps.hint: Your king can go to g1.
steps.ifWrong: 5.O-O: the king is safe and the rook can come to e1 later.
steps.ifRight: Next is c3, which prepares d4.

feedback.c2c3: 5.c3 is good too. This repertoire castles first.

steps.text: Black castles too with 5...O-O.
Prepare d4 and take that square from Black's knight.
steps.ifWrong: 6.c3 prepares d4 and controls the d4 square.
steps.ifRight: The centre stays closed for now. h3, Re1 and Nbd2 come next.

steps.text: 6...d6 frees the bishop on c8, which eyes g4.
Stop the pin before it happens.
steps.hint: A rook's pawn can cover g4.
steps.ifWrong: 7.h3 stops ...Bg4, which would pin your knight.
steps.ifRight: Now Re1 and Nbd2 can follow without the pin.

steps.text: 7...h6 stops Ng5 and Bg5.
Back up e4 with a rook.
steps.hint: The rook on f1 has a better square.
steps.ifWrong: 8.Re1 backs up e4 and gets ready for d4 one day.
steps.ifRight: Next the knight on b1 usually travels to d2, f1 and g3.

steps.text: From 3...Bc5: 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3 d6 6.O-O O-O. You have seen this position. Find the move.
steps.ifWrong: 7.h3 takes g4 away from Black's bishop.

lessons.title: Against ...h6: b4 and a4
lessons.summary: A slow ...h6 lets you gain space on the queenside.

steps.text: 6...h6 stops Ng5 and Bg5, but it does nothing in the centre.
Gain queenside space and chase the bishop.
7...Bb6 keeps the bishop aimed at f2.
Threaten to trap the bishop.
steps.ifWrong: 8.a4 threatens a5, and the bishop on b6 would have no good square.

steps.text: Black can also play 5...h6 before castling.
Keep the same plan: prepare d4 or b4.
steps.ifWrong: 6.c3 first, ready for d4 or b4.
steps.ifRight: ...h6 only stopped Bg5 and Ng5. Your plan is unchanged.

steps.text: Black plays 5...d6 before castling. The bishop on c8 eyes g4. Find the move.
steps.ifWrong: 6.h3 stops the pin before it happens.
steps.ifRight: Then c3, Re1 and Nbd2, the same plan as before.

lessons.title: Against 4...d5 and 4...h6
lessons.summary: Take on d5 and castle; meet slow moves by developing.

steps.text: 4...d5 opens the centre, but you are ready for it.
Take the pawn.
steps.ifWrong: 5.exd5 takes the pawn that attacks your bishop.
steps.ifRight: Black takes back with the knight.

steps.text: 5...Nxd5 puts the knight in the centre.
Make your king safe first.
steps.ifWrong: 6.O-O, and Re1 will put pressure on e5.
steps.ifRight: Later, chase the knight on d5 with c3 and d4, or with Nc3.

steps.text: 4...h6 is slow. It stops Ng5 but develops nothing.
Bring out another piece.
steps.ifRight: Castling comes next; there is no hurry.

feedback.e1g1: Castling is fine. This repertoire brings out 5.Nc3 first, then castles.

steps.text: Black plays the modest 4...Be7. Find a calm move that makes your king safe.
steps.ifWrong: 5.O-O: against a quiet move, castle and play c3 or Re1.
steps.ifRight: The centre stays closed and both sides manoeuvre.

lessons.title: Against 4...d6: hit f7
lessons.summary: When the f8 bishop is shut in, Ng5 attacks f7 twice.

steps.text: 4...d6 shuts in the bishop on f8. Now only the king guards f7.
Attack f7 with a second piece.
steps.hint: Your knight on f3 can jump towards f7.
steps.ifWrong: 5.Ng5 hits f7 with the knight and the bishop at once.
steps.ifRight: Two attackers on f7, and only the king defends it.

steps.text: 5...d5 blocks the bishop's line to f7.
The same position can come from 3...d6.
Develop calmly and keep e4 protected.
steps.ifRight: Watch what happens if Black now plays ...Nf6.

feedback.d2d4: 4.d4 is good too. This repertoire stays calm with 4.d3.

steps.text: 4...Nf6 develops, but it brings back the position from before.
Here 3...d6 4.d3 Nf6 was played. Find the attacking move.
steps.hint: Put a second attacker on f7.
steps.ifWrong: 5.Ng5 attacks f7 with the knight and the bishop.
steps.ifRight: Same position, same idea: f7 is weak while the f8 bishop is shut in.
